items.followUp: What is quinine, and from which plant is it obtained?

rubric.why: Identifies Cinchona as the source plant for quinine.
rubric.description: Cinchona is a tree whose bark contains quinine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Cinchona as a tree or naming its bark.

rubric.why: Names the important product of Cinchona and its medicinal use.
rubric.description: Quinine from Cinchona bark is used to treat malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that quinine is used to treat malaria.

modelAnswer: Cinchona is a tree whose bark contains quinine.
Quinine is a medicine used to treat malaria.

items.followUp: What feature distinguishes rough endoplasmic reticulum from smooth endoplasmic reticulum?

rubric.why: Identifies the feature that gives rough ER its appearance.
rubric.description: Ribosomes are attached to the surface of rough endoplasmic reticulum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ribosomes are attached to rough ER.

rubric.why: Identifies why smooth ER appears smooth.
rubric.description: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes attached to its surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that smooth ER lacks attached ribosomes.

modelAnswer: Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to its surface, giving it a rough appearance.
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no attached ribosomes and therefore appears smooth.

items.followUp: State one function of chromoplasts and one function of leucoplasts.

rubric.why: States the pigment-related feature of chromoplasts.
rubric.description: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chromoplast pigments or their role in giving colour.

rubric.why: States the colour and storage role of leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying leucoplasts as colourless or as food-storing plastids.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments, which give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.

items.followUp: Name two organizations working to conserve biodiversity in Pakistan.

rubric.why: Names one organization that works for biodiversity protection in Pakistan.
rubric.description: WWF Pakistan is an organization working for biodiversity conservation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming WWF Pakistan or the World Wide Fund for Nature.

accept: international union for conservation of nature
rubric.why: Names another organization working for biodiversity protection in Pakistan.
rubric.description: IUCN Pakistan works for the protection of biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming IUCN Pakistan or the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

modelAnswer: WWF Pakistan (World Wide Fund for Nature) works for biodiversity conservation.
IUCN Pakistan (International Union for Conservation of Nature) also works for the protection of biodiversity.

items.followUp: How does predation by sea stars affect mussel populations and biodiversity?

rubric.why: Identifies the feeding relationship between sea stars and mussels.
rubric.description: Sea stars are predators that eat mussels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sea stars or starfish eat mussels.

rubric.why: Explains an ecological effect of sea stars eating mussels.
rubric.description: By controlling mussel numbers, sea stars prevent mussels from dominating and help maintain biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that predation controls mussel numbers or helps maintain biodiversity.

modelAnswer: Sea stars are predators that eat mussels.
By controlling the mussel population, sea stars help prevent mussels from dominating and help maintain biodiversity.

items.followUp: Give two examples of how apoptosis benefits a multicellular organism.

rubric.why: States that apoptosis removes cells that are damaged, abnormal or no longer needed.
rubric.description: Apoptosis removes damaged, abnormal or unnecessary cells from the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a type of cell apoptosis removes.

rubric.why: Gives a further benefit of programmed cell death.
rubric.description: Apoptosis supports normal development and tissue maintenance, and helps prevent abnormal cells from growing uncontrollably.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit, such as development, tissue maintenance or prevention of abnormal cell growth.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis removes damaged, abnormal or unnecessary cells from the body.
It is important in normal development and tissue maintenance, and helps prevent abnormal cells from growing uncontrollably.
